title: Dependency Quarantine Service (DQS) and staged eviction playbook for downstream resilience
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Problem: Intermittent downstream resource degradation (Redis replicas, Kafka brokers, and DB read replicas) can cause cascading tail latency and error amplification across tenant workloads. Current blunt circuit-breakers evict entire hosts quickly, resulting in cache misses, reconnections, and mass reroutes that spike other regions. We need a more surgical approach that isolates bad targets, progressively reduces traffic, and re-admits healthy targets without causing thundering-herd effects.

Proposal: Implement a Dependency Quarantine Service (DQS) as a lightweight control plane component integrated with the runtime routing layer and connection pool manager. DQS computes per-target health scores from multi-signal telemetry, enforces graded admission/pacing policies, coordinates multi-region weight shifts for failover, and drives graceful eviction/recovery probes. The goal is to maintain tenant SLOs (p50/p95 latency and error budgets) while minimizing collateral load during failovers.
acceptance_criteria: DQS publishes downstream.health_score and downstream.quarantine_state (OK|PROBING|QUARANTINED|EVICTED) to metrics and internal trace spans
Runtime routing honors DQS recommendations for >=95% of requests after rollout (config flag to opt-in)
Reduction in cross-host error amplification during chaos tests: mean p95 increase <= 10% compared to baseline for simulated single-host outage
Automated recovery probe mechanism re-admits healthy targets without manual intervention in >=90% of tests
design_notes: Health scoring inputs: sliding 1m error rate, 5m p95 latency relative to baseline, connection queue depth, socket errors per-second, GC/CPU saturation tags from host agent, recent eviction history (decay weight)

Score computation: weighted sum with adaptive coefficients. Example: health_score = 100 - (w1*err_rate_pct + w2*latency_pct_over_baseline + w3*conn_queue_norm + w4*socket_err_norm). Normalized 0-100 where lower is worse.

Graded circuit modes: MONITOR -> PROBING (serve 5-10% sample of traffic + async shadow) -> SOFT_QUARANTINE (limit concurrency and token-bucket rate) -> QUARANTINE (drain existing conns, direct new requests to fallback) -> EVICT (remove host from routing pool). Each transition has TTL and exponential backoff for retries.

Quarantine behavioral details: in SOFT_QUARANTINE we keep a warm, tiny connection pool to allow lightweight probes and avoid cold-start cache misses; SOFT_QUARANTINE preserves stale reads for read-heavy DB replicas where acceptable by tenant-level policy.
Re-admission logic: periodic canary probes at low concurrency and shadow traffic, requiring consecutive successful probe windows (configurable, default 3) before MONITOR state restored.

Multi-region failover coordination: DQS issues region-level weight deltas rather than instant full traffic shifts. Weight shift uses a ramp function over N seconds (configurable per SLO) and per-tenant slope limits to avoid sending large tenant traffic bursts to a single region.

Connection pool integration: expose per-target min/max pool sizes, warm-pool countdown on quarantine, and immediate soft-drain with graceful in-flight completion. Pool should emit drain_start and drain_complete events for tracing.
Compatibility: DQS exposes an API for Redwood Dedicated and Private control planes; runtime can run a local agent that caches DQS decisions for offline mode with short TTLs.
Operational UX: Console must show quarantined targets, historical health_score graph, and a link to runbook actions (force-evict, trigger-probe, postpone-quarantine).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2w): Implement health_score aggregator in runtime telemetry pipeline. Add metric names downstream.health_score and downstream.signal_* for debugging. Unit tests for score stability under synthetic noise.

Phase 2 (3w): Implement DQS control plane service with a REST/gRPC API. Integrate with routing layer: routing checks DQS decision cache before picking target. Add feature flag runtime.dqs.enabled=false by default.
Phase 3 (2w): Connection pool changes: introduce soft-drain, warm-mini-pools, and per-target concurrency caps. Add events and traces for drain lifecycle.
Phase 4 (2w): Multi-region weight shifter and rollout algorithms. Implement tenant slope limits and per-tenant failover policies.
Phase 5 (1w): Console dashboards and runbook actions. End-to-end integration tests and chaos scenarios.
Phase 6 (1w): Gradual canary rollout to 10% of traffic, evaluate metrics, then 50% and full rollout if stable.
rollout_plan: Opt-in canary: enable runtime.dqs.enabled for internal staging clusters and 2 low-risk customers
Monitor: 72h of canary, check downstream.quarantine_count and tenant SLO regressions. If quarantine_count spikes unexpectedly, rollback config flag and revert pool changes.
Expand: 10% production traffic -> 50% -> 100% over successive days with automated stop criteria based on SLO and error budget triggers
Emergency rollback: feature flag to disable DQS globally and API to set per-cluster allowlist for force-fallback mode
monitoring_and_alerting: Primary metrics to emit: downstream.health_score, downstream.quarantine_state (numeric), downstream.recovery_probe_success_rate, connpool.drain_count, connpool.active_connections_per_host
Alert: downstream.quarantine_count > 5 within 5m in a single region (warning), > 15 within 5m (critical)
Alert: p95 latency increase > 20% for >10m after DQS rollout (critical)
Create dashboard that overlays health_score, host-level CPU/mem, and host agent socket error signals for quick triage
testing_plan: Unit tests for health_score under controlled input distributions
Integration tests: simulate noisy host (spikes in p95 and socket errors) and verify DQS transitions through MONITOR->PROBING->SOFT_QUARANTINE->QUARANTINE as expected
Chaos tests in staging: sequentially quarantine 1 host in a region and validate multi-region ramp maintains SLOs (scripted harness will record p50/p95 errors and throughput)
Replay tests: run previous incident traces through DQS to verify reduced cascade in >90% of scenarios
Customer simulation: run tenant-weighted traffic with per-tenant slope limits to ensure no single tenant overwhelms fallback region
dependencies: ENG-672410 (tenant socket budgeter) - integration for per-tenant slope limits
infra/host-agent (agent-metrics v3) - to provide socket and resource signals
console-team: dashboard widgets and runbook links
runbook_snippets: Force-evict a host: POST /dqs/v1/hosts/{host}/action {"action":"evict"} (requires admin token)
Drain: set connpool.target_state={"host":"soft_drain"} then monitor connpool.drain_complete event
If cross-region latency spikes after failover: reduce region weight by 30% and open temporary canary route to a second fallback region; contact on-call infra and database owners
